'''Anthony Christopher Davison''' (born 28 February 1958)<ref name="CV" /> is a British mathematical statistician and educator. He made seminal contributions to [[extreme value theory]], [[Likelihoodist statistics|likelihood inference]] and [[environmental statistics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Davison (EPF Lausanne): Accurate Directional Inference for Vector Parameters |url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/events/96897/anthony-davison-epf-lausanne-accurate-directional-inference-for-vector-parameters/ |access-date=2023-12-03 |website=Imperial College London |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=intro />

== Education and career ==
Davison was born in London. He attended the [[Warwick School]], followed by the [[St John's College, Oxford|St. John's College, University of Oxford]], where he obtained a B.A. in mathematics in 1980. He then studied at the [[Imperial College London]] and obtained a MSc in statistics in 1981 with a project supervised by [[Martin Beale]]. He went on the obtain a PhD in statistics in 1984 at the [[Imperial College London]] under the supervision of environmental scientist [[Helen ApSimon]] and statistician Richard L. Smith. Between 1984 and 1986, Davison was an assistant professor at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in the United States. He was a lecturer at the Department of Mathematics at the Imperial College London from 1986 to 1989, and a university lecturer at the [[University of Oxford]] from 1989 to 1996.<ref name=CV />

Davison joined [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL) in Switzerland in 1996 as a professor of statistics. He became the chair of the statistics department.<ref name=CV>{{cite web |title=A. C. Davison Full CV |url=https://www.scribd.com/document/354997497/Davison-Full-Cv |via=Scribd |language=en}}</ref> In 2021, Davison, [[Holger Rootzén]] and other published work using the longevity data and [[extreme value theory]] to predict the age limit of humans.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Belzile |first1=Léo R. |last2=Davison |first2=Anthony C. |last3=Rootzén |first3=Holger |last4=Zholud |first4=Dmitrii |year=2021 |title=Human mortality at extreme age |journal=Royal Society Open Science |language=en |volume=8 |issue=9 |doi=10.1098/rsos.202097 |issn=2054-5703|doi-access=free |pmid=34631116 |pmc=8479337 |arxiv=2001.04507 |bibcode=2021RSOS....802097B }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Belzile |first1=Léo R. |last2=Davison |first2=Anthony C. |last3=Gampe |first3=Jutta |last4=Rootzén |first4=Holger |last5=Zholud |first5=Dmitrii |date=7 March 2022 |title=Is There a Cap on Longevity? == Honours and awards ==
Davison was awarded the [[Guy Medal]] in Silver of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] in 2015.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Papageorgiou |first=Nik |date=20 February 2015 |title=Anthony Davison wins Guy Medal in Silver |url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/anthony-davison-wins-guy-medal-in-silver/ |language=en}}</ref> He gave the Medallion lecture of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics {{!}} Le Cam, Neyman and Medallion Lecture previews |url=https://imstat.org/2018/05/15/le-cam-neyman-and-medallion-lecture-previews/ |access-date=2023-12-03 |language=en}}</ref> He is a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]], the Institute of Mathematical Statistics, and the International Statistical Institute.<ref name=intro>{{Cite web |title=EPFL People Anthony Davison |url=https://people.epfl.ch/anthony.davison |access-date=2023-12-03 |website=EPFL People}}</ref>
